Passes when: Names the specific cause of the change, identified well enough that a reviewer could look it up: which customer, vendor, contract, hire or event, and what changed with it. Fails when the cause is a category ("timing", "growth", "higher volume"), even with an amount or dates attached, or when the only name given is where the cost was booked or who billed it.
Feedback when failed: Name the specific vendor, contract, hire, customer, or event that drove this movement.
Why it matters: A category can't be checked; a driver can
Example of good: Up $65K: Bluewater Health's one-time backfill ran on our Stratus Compute account (invoice SC-0731).

Passes when: Says what changed in the business, not only which account moved
Feedback when failed: Tell me what changed in the business, not just which account moved.
Why it matters: The reviewer already sees what moved
Example of good: Down $25K because we paused the pipeline-monitoring campaign after two quarters of high cost per lead.

Passes when: States whether the driver repeats next period
Feedback when failed: Will this repeat next period? Say whether it's one-time or recurring.
Example of good: One-time: the backfill finished Jul 19, so August returns to the run rate.

Passes when: References something a reviewer could pull: invoice, JE, contract, headcount report
Feedback when failed: Point me to something I can pull: the invoice, JE, contract, or headcount report.
Why it matters: Makes the review a check, not a conversation
Example of good: See Stratus invoice SC-0731 and JE 7-114.

Passes when: Gives an amount or share for each driver named, or says what is still unexplained
Feedback when failed: Put a number on each driver, or say how much is still unexplained.
Why it matters: Gives the arithmetic check something to test and makes a partial explanation visible
Example of good: Orion Freight $135K, Cobalt seats $41K, renewal uplifts $12K: $188K in total.

Passes when: Adds something beyond the figures already in the row: more than the account name, the direction of the change, and its size
Feedback when failed: This repeats the numbers already in the row. Tell me what happened, not what moved.
Why it matters: The row already shows the numbers
Example of good: Names what happened (a customer backfill, a price change), not just that hosting rose $65K.

Passes when: The amounts cited for the drivers sum to the variance, within the tolerance in Settings (rule in code; not editable here)
Feedback when failed: The amounts you cite don't add up to the variance. Check each driver's amount, or say how much is still unexplained.
Why it matters: A partial or mistyped explanation should be visible before review
Example of good: Drivers of $52K and $13K for a $65K variance.

Passes when: The commentary is not identical to another line's in the same close (rule in code; not editable here)
Feedback when failed: This is word for word the same as another line. Explain what drove this account specifically.
Example of good: Each line names its own driver.

Passes when: The commentary is not nearly identical to another line's; similarity threshold in Settings (rule in code)
Feedback when failed: This reads almost the same as another line. Make sure it explains this account's movement, not a shared template.
Why it matters: Templates hide the differences between accounts
Example of good: Two salary lines that each name their own hires.
